blocks.text: Onboarding a GitLab group to AI Security Admin Portal connects your organization’s GitLab environment (enterprise, organizations, and projects) to the AI Security Admin Portal. This connection enables AI Security to discover, assess, and help you govern AI-related activity and risks across your codebase.
Before you begin, create a GitLab access token based on your use case. You can create the following types of tokens:

blocks.item: Personal Access Token
Personal token access is suitable for demos or proof-of-concept use only. It provides access to repositories the token owner has access to. To learn more, refer to GitLab Docs.
Group Access Token

A group access token is tied to a specific GitLab group and provides access to all repositories within that group. This is the recommended authentication method. If the token is created at the parent group level, it provides access to all underlying subgroups and their repositories. If the token is created at a subgroup level, access is limited to repositories within that subgroup only. To create a group access token, do the following:
Log in to Gitlab portal.
Go to your Group, and select Settings > Access tokens.
See image.
Click Add Group Access token.
In the Group access tokens page, enter the following:
Token name: Enter a suitable name.
Token description: Provide a suitable description for the token.
Expiration date: Set the expiration date.
Select Roles: Select the following from the drop-down menu.
For SCM Scanning: Reporter.
For PR-Based Scanning: Maintainer.
Select Scopes: Set the scope to define the token's permission levels:
For SCM Scanning: read_api and read_repository.
For PR-Based Scanning: api, read_api, read_repository, and write_repository.
See image.
Click Create group access token.
Copy the token and paste in the AI Security Admin Portal Onboarding GitLab - Access Token field.

blocks.text: To onboard a GitLab group, do the following:

blocks.item: Go to Administration > Account Onboarding.
Click + Add New.
The Start Onboarding window appears.
Select Code Repository.
See image.
In the Select Code Repository window, select the GitLab tile.
See image.
In the Add GitLab Group window, enter the following details.
Integration Alias: Enter a user-friendly name to identify this integration.
GitLab Host: Displays gitlab.com by default. This field is non-editable, as only public GitLab is supported.
Token Type: Select one of the following:
Personal Access Token: To provide access to repositories the token owner has access to.
Group Access Token: To create a group access token that is tied to a specific GitLab group and to provide access to all repositories within that group.
Access Token: Enter the group access token created in your GitLab Group in the GitLab portal.
See image.
Click Save.
Zscaler creates the integration and begins discovering repositories under the configured group.
